flawed_step: Step 1: choosing an edge (or otherwise assuming the graph has an edge or is connected) is unjustified. The hypothesis permits edgeless and disconnected graphs.
counterexample: A graph consisting of two isolated vertices has no edges, so the hypothesis holds vacuously, but it has no universal vertex.
assessment_summary: The proof attempt stops immediately because the premise does not imply that the graph has any edges or is connected; therefore the claimed conclusion is false under the stated conventions.
